candidates.statement: The purpose of this guidance is to provide recommendations to industry, specifically master file 15 holders , 1 regarding where (i.e., to which FDA center) to submit a master file (MF): 2 , 3 (1) that is 16 referenced in and intended to support more than one regulatory submission for which the lead 17 center (i.e., the center that has primary review responsibility 4 ) for those submissions may vary, 18 or (2) where the information in the MF may need to be accessed and reviewed by more than one 19 FDA center to support review of the referencing submission(s) (e.g., MFs referenced by 20 combination product submissions). When an MF would be accessed by more than one center, it 21 is referred to as a cross-center MF . These recommendations are intended to help MF holders 22 determine to which center to submit their MF. In turn, this may help MF holders identify any 23 center-specific MF submission recommendations applicable to their situation. 24
candidates.context: Although the general MF concept is similar across the four medical product centers, the 26 recommendations for submitting MFs and the MFs hosted by (i.e., located in) each center have 27 aspects unique to that center (e.g., how to submit, content, format, naming convention, storage 28 system). The recommended hosting center for specific MFs is based on the applications and files 29 the MF is intended to support. This guidance does not provide information about the center- 30 specific recommendations or FDA’s MF review processes. Center-specific information can be 31 found on FDA’s website. 5

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 45 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 46 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 47 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 48 not required. 49
candidates.context: FDA generally discourages MF holders from resubmitting previously submitted MFs that do not 41 reflect the recommendations in this draft guidance. The recommendations provided, once 42 finalized, are for new MF submissions going forward. 43

candidates.statement: Applicants and sponsors can cross-reference an MF that resides in any medical product center, 119 making it possible to reference the information it contains without the applicants and sponsors 120 having access to its contents. Historically, this has raised questions about which center should 121 receive an MF to be referenced by submissions across multiple centers. For example, when MFs 122 contain information about the device constituent part of a CDER-led combination product, some 123 MF holders have submitted the MF to CDER and others to CDRH. Although the MF can be 124 referenced by a CDER-led combination product submission regardless of its hosting center, 125 establishing a consistent process for designating which center should receive these MFs is 126 expected to enhance efficiency for both MF holders and FDA reviewers. 127

candidates.statement: Based on this information, the two subsections that follow outline FDA’s recommendations for 144 determining the hosting center of the MF (see Appendix for examples of FDA’s 145 recommendations). 9 There may be scenarios in which the MF holder does not have sufficient 146 information to determine to which center an MF should be submitted. MF holders can engage 147 FDA if they cannot determine the appropriate hosting center for an MF. 148
candidates.context: • Whether the MF will support a combination product submission. 142 9 Exceptions may occur and are handled on a case-by-case basis.

candidates.statement: When an MF contains information that will support a regulatory submission for a combination 152 product, the recommended hosting center is generally determined based on the lead center and 153 which constituent part is the subject of the MF. MFs that will be referenced by regulatory 154 submissions for combination products should typically include information about only one 155 constituent part of the combination product. 156
candidates.context: A. Recommendations for Where to Submit Master Files Supporting Regulatory 149 Submissions for Combination Products 150 • If an MF contains information about the constituent part of a CBER-led combination 158 product, CBER is the recommended hosting center, regardless of whether the information 159 is related to a biological product, drug, or device constituent part. 160

candidates.statement: In rare cases, the constituent parts of a combination product may be marketed under two 178 applications in two different centers. In this scenario, when an MF contains information that will 179 support one of the constituent parts, the recommended hosting center of the MF is the center that 180 will be receiving the referencing submission for that constituent part. For example, if a 181 combination product is composed of a drug constituent part being marketed under an NDA and a 182 device constituent part being marketed under a premarket approval application (PMA), an MF 183 referenced by the NDA should be submitted to the center receiving the NDA and an MF 184 referenced by the PMA should be submitted to the center receiving the PMA. 185
candidates.context: 10 On June 30, 2003, FDA transferred some of the therapeutic biological products that had been reviewed and regulated by CBER to CDER.
